title: Impact of Additional Representative on Public Spending

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD). This is appropriate because districts receive a second representative based on crossing a population threshold, creating a discontinuous assignment rule. The key assumption is that districts just below and above the threshold are similar in all unobserved characteristics except for the treatment (having a second representative), allowing us to estimate the causal effect by comparing outcomes at the discontinuity.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(rdrobust)
library(ggplot2)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s99_data.csv")

# The cutoff appears to be at running_var = 0 (since treatment changes around there)
# Let's verify this by examining the data
cutoff <- 0

# Main RDD analysis using rdrobust
rdd_result <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff)
print("Main RDD Results:")
print(summary(rdd_result))

# Extract and print the treatment effect
treatment_effect <- rdd_result$coef[1]
se <- rdd_result$se[1]
pvalue <- rdd_result$pv[1]

cat("\n=== MAIN RESULT ===\n")
cat("Treatment Effect (Additional Representative):", round(treatment_effect, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(se, 4), "\n")
cat("P-value:", round(pvalue, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(treatment_effect - 1.96*se, 4), ",", round(treatment_effect + 1.96*se, 4), "]\n")

# Robustness checks
cat("\n=== ROBUSTNESS CHECKS ===\n")

# 1. Different bandwidth
rdd_half_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff, h = rdd_result$bws[1]/2)
cat("Half bandwidth - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_half_bw$coef[1], 4), 
    ", P-value:", round(rdd_half_bw$pv[1], 4), "\n")

rdd_double_bw <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff, h = rdd_result$bws[1]*2)
cat("Double bandwidth - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_double_bw$coef[1], 4), 
    ", P-value:", round(rdd_double_bw$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# 2. Different polynomial orders
rdd_linear <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 1)
cat("Linear polynomial - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_linear$coef[1], 4), 
    ", P-value:", round(rdd_linear$pv[1], 4), "\n")

rdd_cubic <- rdrobust(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff, p = 3)
cat("Cubic polynomial - Treatment Effect:", round(rdd_cubic$coef[1], 4), 
    ", P-value:", round(rdd_cubic$pv[1], 4), "\n")

# 3. Density test (McCrary test)
density_test <- rddensity(data$running_var, c = cutoff)
cat("Density test p-value:", round(density_test$test$p_jk, 4), "\n")

# Visualization
# Create RDD plot
rdplot_result <- rdplot(data$y, data$running_var, c = cutoff,
                       title = "RDD: Effect of Additional Representative on Public Spending",
                       x.label = "Population (Running Variable)",
                       y.label = "Public Spending per Capita")

# Print sample sizes
cat("\n=== SAMPLE INFORMATION ===\n")
cat("Total observations:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Treated (above cutoff):", sum(data$treated), "\n")
cat("Control (below cutoff):", sum(1 - data$treated), "\n")
cat("Effective observations (within bandwidth):", rdd_result$N_h[1] + rdd_result$N_h[2], "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive treatment effect of approximately 0.2-0.4 increase in public spending per capita. The reasoning is that districts with an additional representative likely have greater political influence and bargaining power in securing public resources. Representatives typically advocate for their constituents and compete for government funding, so having two representatives instead of one should lead to increased ability to secure public spending. The magnitude should be economically meaningful but not extremely large, as there are budget constraints and diminishing returns to additional political representation.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Exploit the population threshold for a second representative as a cutoff for treatment assignment.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The presence of a second representative decreases public spending per capita.
